The requester authorizes separate random complex photo tests with an attached portrait. The coordinator assigns this arm a small-grocery comparison test; the product pair and staging are independently randomized and agent-authored, not requester-specified.

A candid editorial photograph in a tiny neighborhood grocery on a dry overcast morning. One adult woman shopper stands close to a low wooden shelf of cooking oils, comparing two similar olive oil bottles in a single visible moment of choice. Her left hand holds a green glass olive oil bottle and her right hand holds an amber glass olive oil bottle; she brings their front labels side by side at chest height, angles both labels toward herself, and studies them with a concentrated downward gaze. The bottles remain separate and equally visible, with the colored glass and matching olive oil bottle shapes making their similarity and difference clear. Her long dark wavy hair parted near the center, dark eyes, and softly contoured face take only visible appearance guidance from the attached portrait. She wears a charcoal cardigan over a simple pale shirt. A blue wire shopping basket rests on the counter below her elbows. Narrow shelves of bottled sauces continue behind her, while cool fluorescent strips and gray window light define the compact working shop. Frame her face, both hands, both bottle bodies and labels, the basket, and the shelves together in an eye-level three-quarter photograph; preserve plausible grips, supported posture, and crisp product-to-hand contact.
